## Headline

The three notes files now pass the banned-word check and the long-sentence check.

First, notes/a.md no longer contains a booster.
Second, notes/b.md is now three short sentences with the same outage facts.
Third, notes/c.md no longer contains a booster and keeps the worker sequence.

## Background

Three notes files failed a style check. One file had a booster, one file had a long sentence, and one file had both. The request was a procedure, then a fix of each file in order.

## Relevance

A later agent can follow the procedure without a guess about tool order. The notes keep their facts, so the check can pass without a meaning change.

## Information

This section covers the checks, the assumption, and the alternative.

Before the rewrite, notes/a.md failed on one booster [1]. notes/b.md failed on one sentence over 25 words [2]. notes/c.md failed on both a booster and sentence length [3]. Therefore, each file needed a rewrite that kept the same facts. After the rewrite, each of the three files reports zero failures [4]. Confidence is high, three tool checks after the rewrite.

Assumption: A booster before faster adds no speed number. Why not measured: The material does not state it. Validate by: time both parsers on one log. If wrong: the note can misstate the gain.

The strongest alternative is to keep the long outage sentence. It loses because the length check still fails [2].

## End

I recommend that we close the edit with three reads, in file order.

1. Test:
Given the saved release note,
When a reader checks the speed line,
Then it still says two seconds.
Read notes/a.md once. This removes the risk of a lost speed fact. Domain: Clear, because a known rule decides the result. Kind: deterministic.

2. Test:
Given the saved incident note,
When a reader checks the fallback lines,
Then the text still says one hour.
Read notes/b.md once. This removes the risk of a lost duration fact. Domain: Clear, because a known rule decides the result. Kind: deterministic. Step 2 MUST NOT start until the test in Step 1 passes.

3. Test:
Given the saved design note,
When a reader checks the last lines,
Then a worker still marks the message done.
Read notes/c.md once. This removes the risk of a lost worker step. Domain: Clear, because a known rule decides the result. Kind: deterministic. Step 3 MUST NOT start until the test in Step 2 passes.

## Follow-up

If a later edit adds a booster or a long sentence, run the procedure again.

[2] check_file result for notes/b.md before the rewrite, this session, 2026-11-06. [P]

[4] check_file results for notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md after the rewrite, this session, 2026-11-06. [P]

# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences

Use this procedure on one notes file. The tools are list_files, read_file, write_file, and check_file.

1. Call list_files. Confirm the target path is present.
2. Call read_file on the target path. Copy the meaning of each sentence before you edit.
3. Call check_file on the target path. Record each banned word and each sentence over 25 words.
4. Rewrite the file. Remove each banned word. Split each long sentence. Keep the same facts.
5. Call write_file with the full new text. Do not append.
6. Call check_file again. If it still reports a banned word or a long sentence, repeat steps 4 to 6.
7. Stop when check_file reports no banned words and no sentences over 25 words.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service then used the database for every request. That fallback lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. It writes the result to the store. It then marks the message as done. No other worker picks that message up again.
